overview.description: Gaple is a popular Indonesian block domino game played on a single train line. Players add matching tiles at either end, and if blocked they either discard a dead tile or pass depending on table rules.

history.origins: Gaple developed as an Indonesian local form of block dominoes using western double-six tiles.
timeline: 20th century: Gaple spread widely through social play in Indonesian communities.
Modern era: It remains one of the most common casual domino games in Indonesia.
history.evolution: Local rules preserved the single-train structure but developed distinct blocked-hand and dead-tile handling.
history.cultural: Gaple is a staple social game and is often played in informal money or chip settlements.

setup.players: Four or five players. With four, play can be individual or partnerships; with five, individual play.
setup.dealing: Four-player variants use either 6 each (4 face-down in center) or 7 each (no center tiles). Five-player game deals 5 each (3 face-down in center).

rules.objective: Be left with the lowest pip total when the hand ends, either by going out or by blocked play.
rules.gameplay: Play proceeds on a single train, adding one matching tile to either open end. In hands with undealt center tiles, one center tile is exposed to start the line. In 4-player 7-tile play, the double blank 0-0 starts the first hand and later hands begin with a double from the previous winner side. A blocked player usually discards one dead tile face down; some tables use pass-only handling.
keyRules: Unplayed tiles, including dead tiles, count as penalty pips at hand end.
Common tie-breaker: lowest single tile wins ties on total pips; if still tied, lowest end wins.
Some tables count the double blank 0-0 as 25 only when no other blank tile remains in that hand.

strategy.basic: Unload high-pip doubles early; stranded heavy tiles are costly in blocked endings.
strategy.intermediate: Track which pip numbers are saturated to predict blocked ends and preserve flexible connectors.
strategy.advanced: In dead-tile play, choose dead discards that minimize your own penalty while reducing opponents' line options.
tips: Remember there are seven copies of each pip number in a double-six set.
When low on options, protect low-value singles for tie-break situations.
Adjust aggression based on whether blocked players discard dead tiles or simply pass.

list.name: Four Player Six-Tile Deal
list.description: Each player takes six tiles, leaving four face down; one center tile is exposed to start.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Deal size and center-tile setup differ from base; engine overrides not yet mapped.

list.name: Pass-Only Blocking
list.description: When blocked, players pass and keep all tiles in hand instead of discarding dead tiles.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Blocked-hand branch (pass vs discard) is procedural; no engine constant overrides needed.

list.name: Double-Blank 25 Rule
list.description: At scoring, the double blank 0-0 counts 25 only if the player holds no other blank tile.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Optional scoring rule for 0-0; scoring override not yet mapped to engine.

difficulty.easy: Plays legal matches but fails to manage pip totals and dead-tile risk.
difficulty.medium: Balances line control with pip reduction and recognizes blocked-board threats.
difficulty.hard: Counts exposed numbers, optimizes endgame tie-breakers, and adapts to pass versus dead-tile rules.

considerations: AI policy must support both blocked-hand branches: dead-tile discard and pass-only variation.

legal.reasonForNA: Traditional Indonesian folk domino game; no documented IP holder or public domain claim.

phases.label: Deal Tiles
phases.notes: Deal by chosen table variant: 4 players (6 each with 4 center tiles or 7 each), or 5 players (5 each with 3 center tiles).

phases.label: Line Play
phases.notes: Players match open ends. In dead-tile rules, blocked players discard one hidden tile; in pass rules, they pass.

phases.label: Score Deal
phases.notes: Count pips on all unplayed tiles, including dead tiles. Lowest total wins, with tie-breakers.

ante.reason: Gaple has no ante payment in its standard rules.

deal.description: Deal tiles according to selected 4-player or 5-player Gaple variant.
deal.constraints: Dealer only at the start of each deal.

reveal_market.reason: No market area exists in Gaple.

buy_market.reason: Tiles are never purchased from market in this domino game.

buy_stock.reason: There is no stock buy action because all tiles are dealt out.

fold.reason: Players remain active until go out or blocked end; fold is not used.

check.reason: No betting rounds exist where checking would apply.

call.reason: Gaple has no call mechanic and no wager matching.

bet.reason: The game has no betting system.

raise.reason: No betting system exists, so raising is not applicable.

declare.reason: Gaple has no declaration phase in standard rules.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands are not formally revealed as an action before scoring.

award_pot.description: Apply end-of-hand pip scoring and tie-breakers for lowest hand.

play_card.description: Play one tile to a legal open end of the domino line.
play_card.constraints: Tile must match the pip value at one open line end.

draw.reason: No drawing occurs after the initial deal because there is no boneyard.

discard.description: Discard one tile face down as a dead tile when blocked, if using dead-tile rules.
discard.constraints: Only valid when no legal play exists and table uses dead-tile variant.

pass.description: Pass when you have no tile that matches either open end of the line.
pass.constraints: Only legal when no playable match exists.

meld.reason: This domino variant does not use meld declarations.

go_out.description: End the deal by playing your last remaining tile.
go_out.constraints: Triggers immediately when a legal play empties hand.

edgeCases.text: In the dead-tile variant, a blocked player discards one hidden dead tile instead of passing; dead tiles count in scoring.
Some tables count [0-0] as 25 only when the player has no other unplayed tile containing a blank.

customLogicNeeded: Support three common deal structures: 4p-6 tiles, 4p-7 tiles, and 5p-5 tiles.
Apply variant branch when blocked: dead-tile discard versus pure pass.
Implement tie-break by lowest single tile then lowest end.

engine.deckDescription: The deck is a standard double-six domino set of twenty-eight tiles; each tile has two ends with pip values from zero to six, and every combination from 0-0 through 6-6 appears exactly once for line play.
engine.suitDescription: Domino sets do not use traditional card suits; each tile is identified by its two end values (pips from zero to six), and matching is done by connecting ends with the same pip count on the train.
engine.rankDescription: The rank set is Domino_double6: tiles are valued by the pips on each end (zero through six); play uses matching end values to extend the line, and unplayed tile pips count as penalty at hand end.
engine.dealPattern: Deal by local variant: 4p (6 each or 7 each) or 5p (5 each).

hero.title: GAPLE
hero.subtitle: Indonesian Block Dominoes
hero.tagline: Build the line, manage dead tiles, and finish with the lowest pips.

synthesis.shortDescription: Indonesian single-train domino game for four or five players with blocked-hand and dead-tile variants.

prompts.human: Gaple: build the line with matching ends and keep your hand pip total lower than everyone else when the hand ends.
prompts.ai: Game: Gaple. Use a double-six set with 4-5 players. Play one matching tile to either open end each turn. If blocked, either discard a dead tile or pass depending on table rule. Hand ends when someone goes out or line is blocked; lowest pip total wins with tie-break by lowest single tile then lowest end.

scoring.description: At hand end, each player totals pips on all unplayed tiles, including dead tiles if used. Lowest total wins the hand.
scoring.winCondition: Winner is the player with least points; ties are broken by lowest single tile, then lowest end value.

nullReasons.targetScore: Gaple is commonly played hand-by-hand or for agreed stake settlement rather than a universal fixed target.
nullReasons.cardValues: Gaple scores by pip totals on unplayed tiles; there are no card face values.
